title: Itch: A Sense of Its Own

generated.pipeline: extract → Opus draft → Codex accuracy gate and fixes

cards.front: Itch is the unpleasant sensation associated with a desire to {{c1::scratch}}.
cards.quote: Itch is the unpleasant sensation associated with a desire to scratch.

cards.front: A {{c1::pruriceptor}} is a primary sensory neuron that detects itch-producing stimuli.
cards.quote: A pruriceptor is a primary sensory neuron that detects itch-producing stimuli.

cards.front: Why does calling a sensory neuron a pruriceptor depend on an experiment rather than on its molecular marker?
cards.back: The term is functional. A marker only labels cells; it takes an experiment to show what the marked cells do in the tested assays.
cards.quote: The term is functional: a molecular marker is useful only insofar as an experiment shows what the marked cells do.

cards.front: In the mouse experiments of this lesson, what does treating itch as a sense of its own deliberately not claim?
cards.back: It does not make scratching a report of sensation, does not make any marker itch-only under every manipulation, and does not establish the same cell classes in people.
cards.quote: It does not make scratching a report of sensation, make any marker itch-only under every manipulation

cards.front: A light mechanical trigger can evoke scratching in dry or inflamed skin; touch-evoked itch is {{c1::alloknesis}}.
cards.quote: A light mechanical trigger can evoke scratching in dry or inflamed skin; touch-evoked itch is alloknesis.
cards.section: Start at the skin: one sensation, several inputs

cards.front: Where does histamine that causes itch come from in skin, and what blocks most histamine itch in people?
cards.back: Mostly from skin mast cells; it acts on histamine receptors, and H1 antagonists block most histamine itch in people.
cards.quote: Histamine comes mostly from skin mast cells and acts on histamine receptors; H1 antagonists block most histamine itch in people.
cards.section: Start at the skin: one sensation, several inputs

cards.front: In mice, which signalling molecules does histamine itch involve, and deficiency of which channel markedly reduces chloroquine and BAM8-22 scratching?
cards.back: Histamine itch involves PLC-beta-3 and TRPV1. Chloroquine and BAM8-22 scratching is markedly reduced in Trpa1-deficient mice.
cards.why: Not all chemical itch is histaminergic, and the routes differ downstream of the receptor.
cards.quote: In mice, histamine itch involves PLC-beta-3 and TRPV1 (Imamachi and colleagues, PNAS, 2009)
cards.section: Start at the skin: one sensation, several inputs

cards.front: In a made-up mouse experiment, an H1 antagonist abolishes scratching to histamine but leaves chloroquine scratching unchanged, and chloroquine scratching is markedly reduced in Trpa1-deficient mice. What does this show about chemical itch?
cards.back: Chemical itch has more than one route: chloroquine acts through a different receptor and channel pathway than histamine does, so blocking one receptor leaves the other route intact.
cards.quote: Not all chemical itch is histaminergic, and the routes differ downstream of the receptor.
cards.section: Start at the skin: one sensation, several inputs

cards.front: Deleting Trpv1 does not remove chloroquine calcium responses from cultured mouse sensory neurons, even though those neurons carry TRPV1. What inference does this block?
cards.back: It blocks the inference from expression to use: a neuron that carries a channel need not use that channel for every input, so channel expression alone does not assign a transduction route.
cards.quote: Carrying a channel does not mean using it for every input.
cards.section: Start at the skin: one sensation, several inputs

cards.front: Are chemical and mechanical itch assigned to mutually exclusive peripheral cell types in the mouse work covered here?
cards.back: No. They use partly different spinal circuits, but they are not assigned to mutually exclusive peripheral cell types.
cards.quote: Chemical and mechanical itch use partly different spinal circuits, although they are not assigned to mutually exclusive peripheral cell types.
cards.section: Start at the skin: one sensation, several inputs

cards.front: What is a strict labelled line?
cards.back: A pathway whose activity means one thing regardless of how it is activated.
cards.quote: A strict labelled line is a pathway whose activity means one thing regardless of how it is activated.
cards.section: How far the labelled-line claim can go

cards.front: What does an ablation experiment test, and what does a restricted rescue test instead?
cards.back: Ablation tests necessity in the assays used. A restricted rescue tests what a population can drive under one isolated input.
cards.quote: ablation tests necessity in the assays used, while restricted rescue tests what a population can drive under one isolated input
cards.section: How far the labelled-line claim can go

cards.front: In the MrgprA3 work, deleting the Mrgpr gene cluster and ablating MrgprA3-positive neurons are said to split at different levels. How?
cards.back: Deleting the cluster removes one receptor route. Ablation removes every input through those neurons, which themselves respond to histamine and are needed for normal histamine scratching.
cards.quote: deleting the Mrgpr cluster removes one receptor route, whereas ablation removes every input through those neurons
cards.section: How far the labelled-line claim can go

cards.front: Liu and colleagues (Cell, 2009) deleted a cluster of Mrgpr genes in male mice aged 2 to 3 months. What scratching pattern did they report?
cards.back: Less scratching to chloroquine, with histamine scratching spared.
cards.quote: Liu and colleagues (Cell, 2009) deleted the Mrgpr cluster in male mice aged 2 to 3 months.
cards.section: Ages, treatment schedules and rescue scope

cards.front: After inducible ablation of MrgprA3-positive neurons in adult mice, scratching to several pruritogens including histamine fell while the pain assays tested were unchanged. What is the narrowest correct conclusion?
cards.back: Those neurons are needed for much itch scratching in the assays and ages tested. That is narrower than calling them itch-only neurons.
cards.quote: Those inferences are narrower than "itch-only neuron."
cards.section: How far the labelled-line claim can go

cards.front: The same MrgprA3 population in mice is driven either by fast ionotropic stimulation (light-gated channels or P2X3) or by Gq-linked stimulation. What behaviour follows each, and what does the contrast show?
cards.back: Fast ionotropic drive predominantly evoked nocifensive, pain-related defensive behaviour; Gq-linked stimulation of the same cells evoked itch behaviour. How a population is activated changes the output, which a strict labelled line would not predict.
cards.quote: Gq-linked stimulation of the same MrgprA3 population evoked itch behaviour (Sharif and colleagues, Neuron, 2020).
cards.section: How far the labelled-line claim can go

cards.front: In the restricted TRPV1 rescue of the MrgprA3 experiments, where was functional TRPV1 present, and on what background?
cards.back: Only in MrgprA3-positive neurons, on a Trpv1-null background.
cards.quote: In the rescue, functional TRPV1 existed only in MrgprA3-positive neurons on a Trpv1-null background.
cards.section: How far the labelled-line claim can go

cards.front: The restricted TRPV1 rescue made cheek-injected capsaicin evoke itch-related behaviour in mice. What does that license, and what does it not?
cards.back: It shows that MrgprA3-positive neurons can drive itch-related behaviour when they are the only cells carrying that one input. It does not show the neurons are itch-only, nor what they do when other populations are also activated: the conclusion holds for the driver, age and assays used.
cards.quote: Their restricted TRPV1 rescue then made cheek-injected capsaicin evoke itch-related behaviour.
cards.section: Ages, treatment schedules and rescue scope

cards.front: In transfected HEK293 calcium assays, chloroquine's functional EC50 was 27.55 ± 2.03 µM at mouse MrgprA3 and 297.68 ± 2.10 µM at human MRGPRX1 (mean ± SEM). By what factor do the central estimates differ?
cards.back: 297.68 / 27.55 = 10.81. Chloroquine is about eleven times less potent at the human receptor in this assay.
cards.quote: The functional EC50 was 27.55 ± 2.03 µM at mouse MrgprA3 and 297.68 ± 2.10 µM at human MRGPRX1 (mean ± SEM).
cards.section: Worked problem: potency is not identity

cards.front: Impose a deliberately simple model with unit Hill slope, zero baseline and a maximum of 1, so R(C) = C / (EC50 + C). At 30 µM chloroquine, what response does it give at mouse MrgprA3 (EC50 27.55 µM) and at human MRGPRX1 (EC50 297.68 µM), and is the ratio the 10.81 EC50 ratio?
cards.back: Mouse: 30 / (27.55 + 30) = 30 / 57.55 = 0.521. Human: 30 / (297.68 + 30) = 30 / 327.68 = 0.0916. The response ratio is about 5.69, not 10.81: the response is nonlinear and bounded by its maximum.
cards.quote: The response ratio is about 5.69, not 10.81.
cards.section: Worked problem: potency is not identity

cards.front: Using the same simple model, R(C) = C / (EC50 + C), what chloroquine concentration at human MRGPRX1 (EC50 297.68 µM) gives the response that 30 µM gives at mouse MrgprA3 (EC50 27.55 µM)?
cards.back: The mouse response is 0.521. Solve C / (297.68 + C) = 0.521: C = 297.68 × 0.521 / 0.479 = about 324 µM, which is 10.8 times 30 µM. The EC50 ratio reappears as a concentration ratio at matched response, not as a response ratio at matched concentration.
cards.why: The assumed unit slope and matched maxima are the lesson's simplification, not fitted values.
cards.quote: an EC50 ratio is not a response ratio at every concentration
cards.section: Worked problem: potency is not identity

cards.front: What does a functional EC50 measured in a transfected cell line mean, and what does it not mean?
cards.back: It is functional potency in that assay. It is not binding affinity, neuronal firing, perceived itch, or evidence that mouse and human neurons match.
cards.quote: EC50 here is functional potency in a transfected cell, not binding affinity, neuronal firing, perceived itch
cards.section: Worked problem: potency is not identity

cards.front: In the Mishra and Hoon mouse model of chemical itch, give the functional order of the relay from afferent to spinal output.
cards.back: Afferent Nppb, then NPRA-expressing spinal cells, then GRP and GRPR.
cards.quote: afferent Nppb, then NPRA-expressing spinal cells, then GRP and GRPR (Mishra and Hoon, Science, 2013)
cards.section: What the ordered relay does not settle

cards.front: In the Mishra and Hoon model, which cells supply Nppb?
cards.back: A subset of TRPV1-positive primary sensory neurons, rather than dorsal-horn cells.
cards.quote: Nppb is supplied by a subset of TRPV1-positive primary sensory neurons rather than dorsal-horn cells
cards.section: What the ordered relay does not settle

cards.front: Nppb-null mice lost almost all responses to the itch agents tested, intrathecal Nppb still evoked scratching in them, and GRP still evoked scratching after about 70 percent of NPRA-expressing spinal cells were removed. What ordering do these results support?
cards.back: Nppb acts on NPRA-expressing cells, which lie upstream of GRP and GRPR. The rescue shows the downstream machinery in the nulls can still respond; it does not by itself show direct synapses.
cards.quote: GRP also still evoked scratching after about 70 percent of the spinal cells expressing NPRA, the Nppb receptor, were removed
cards.section: Ages, treatment schedules and rescue scope

cards.front: Name three things the ordered Nppb to NPRA to GRP to GRPR experiments did not establish.
cards.back: They did not demonstrate direct synaptic contacts, did not identify a unique source of GRP, and did not establish the same circuit in humans.
cards.quote: The experiments did not demonstrate direct synaptic contacts, identify a unique source of GRP or establish the same circuit in humans.
cards.section: What the ordered relay does not settle

cards.front: What two independent mouse results support a role for GRPR-expressing spinal neurons in itch?
cards.back: Grpr-mutant mice scratched less to the pruritogens tested while responding normally in the pain assays reported, and ablating GRPR-expressing spinal neurons markedly reduced scratching to the tested pruritogens with no change in the measured pain behaviours.
cards.quote: ablating GRPR-expressing spinal neurons markedly reduced scratching to the tested pruritogens while the measured pain behaviours did not change
cards.section: What the ordered relay does not settle

cards.front: Transcriptomic work places Nppb mainly in the Nppb- and Sst-marked afferent class rather than the MrgprA3 class. What follows for how MrgprA3 afferents reach the dorsal horn?
cards.back: They probably reach GRP neurons by another transmitter, so the Nppb relay is one route into the spinal circuit, not the route from every pruriceptor.
cards.quote: This is one route, not the route from every pruriceptor.
cards.section: What the ordered relay does not settle

cards.front: Bhlhb5-mutant mice, tested mainly at four weeks, scratched excessively, which was linked to loss of a subset of inhibitory interneurons. What does this support, and what limits it?
cards.back: It supports that disinhibition can produce itch-related output. Bhlhb5 is expressed transiently in the developing dorsal spinal cord, so this was not an acute manipulation and the phenotype carries developmental scope.
cards.quote: Disinhibition can therefore produce itch-related output, but this was not an acute manipulation.
cards.section: What the ordered relay does not settle

cards.front: How can counter-stimuli such as pain and menthol, and kappa-opioid agonists, reduce itch?
cards.back: The inhibitory interneurons that respond to counter-itch stimuli release the kappa-opioid peptide dynorphin, and pharmacological evidence places its antipruritic action at GRPR-expressing neurons or farther downstream.
cards.quote: This can help explain why counter-stimuli and kappa-opioid agonists reduce itch, whereas mu agonists can provoke it.
cards.section: What the ordered relay does not settle

cards.front: One study deleted Grp in sensory neurons and found less nonhistaminergic scratching with histamine scratching spared, while its intersectional ablation of spinal Grp neurons did not reduce itch; another laboratory's spinally restricted ablation of GRP neurons did reduce itch. How should this be read?
cards.back: Each result stands for its own tests: targeting strategy, age and reporter coverage differ between them, so the source of the GRP acting on GRPR is unsettled rather than decided by either study.
cards.quote: Albisetti and colleagues (Journal of Neuroscience, 2019) reported the opposite after a spinally restricted ablation of GRP neurons: itch-related behaviour fell.
cards.section: The disputed source of GRP

cards.front: Suppose sensory and spinal sources both release GRP and partly compensate for one another. Which comparison is most likely to expose that redundancy, and why?
cards.back: Compare each source-specific deletion with the combined deletion, then add source-specific rescues. Either single deletion could have only a modest effect even when both sources contribute.
cards.quote: Compare each source-specific deletion with the combined deletion, then add source-specific rescues.
cards.section: The disputed source of GRP

cards.front: Design an experiment to decide which source supplies the GRP acting on GRPR in the mouse dorsal horn. Name the comparisons and the measurements that should carry the weight.
cards.back: Compare sensory-neuron and spinal-neuron Grp deletions in one laboratory, background and age, scoring the same assays with histamine and nonhistaminergic pruritogens; add the combined deletion and source-specific rescues. In each group measure Grp transcript, GRP peptide and release, validating antibodies in Grp-null tissue, and record from GRPR neurons in slices while stimulating each candidate source, with GRPR block as a control. Weigh release and slice measurements most heavily, since behavioural effect sizes need not track each source's peptide contribution.
cards.quote: Record from GRPR neurons in spinal slices while stimulating each candidate source, sensory afferents or spinal GRP neurons.
cards.section: Design problem: where does spinal GRP come from?

cards.front: Ablating or silencing NPY::Cre-lineage, Lbx1-intersected dorsal spinal interneurons in mice raised mechanical itch without a matching rise in the tested chemical itch or pain sensitivity, and the raised scratching persisted after GRPR-cell ablation. What does that support?
cards.back: An inhibitory gate restrains a mechanical itch route that, in that paradigm, does not depend on the chemical GRPR relay.
cards.quote: the raised scratching persisted after GRPR-cell ablation, so in that paradigm it did not depend on the chemical relay
cards.section: Mechanical itch: a partly separate route

cards.front: At postnatal day 30, only 35 percent of NPY::Cre reporter-positive spinal cells still expressed NPY. Does the reporter identify current NPY expression or developmental history?
cards.back: Developmental history. Cre permanently marks cells that passed through the expression state, including cells no longer expressing NPY at the time of testing.
cards.quote: Cre permanently marks cells that passed through the expression state, including cells no longer expressing NPY at the time of testing.
cards.section: Mechanical itch: a partly separate route

cards.front: In one mouse paradigm mechanical itch persisted after GRPR-cell ablation, while another study found Tac2-Cre interneurons receive A-beta input, contact GRPR neurons, and that GRPR-neuron ablation abolished mechanical itch. What should be concluded?
cards.back: GRPR's role in mechanical itch is model-dependent: each result holds for its own targeting strategy and assay, so neither settles whether mechanical itch needs GRPR cells in general.
cards.quote: The role of GRPR remains model-dependent
cards.section: Mechanical itch: a partly separate route

cards.front: Deleting Piezo2 across mouse skin epithelium, or in Merkel cells with an inducible line, increased touch-evoked scratching, and chemogenetic activation of Merkel cells reduced alloknesis in a dry-skin model. Is Merkel-cell Piezo2 signalling a generator or a brake here, and why?
cards.back: A brake: loss raised touch-evoked scratching, whereas activation lowered alloknesis. The loss-of-function and gain-of-function effects run in opposite directions, which is the signature of a restraint. No direct Merkel-to-NPY synapse was shown.
cards.quote: A brake: loss raised touch-evoked scratching, whereas activation lowered alloknesis.
cards.section: Mechanical itch: a partly separate route

cards.front: A later study found that Merkel-cell Piezo2 signalling can promote spontaneous itch in chronic dry skin. Does that overturn the brake result?
cards.back: No. The earlier restraint applies to touch-evoked scratching, not to every itch behaviour, so the two endpoints can differ in the same cells.
cards.quote: The earlier restraint applies to touch-evoked scratching, not every itch behaviour.
cards.section: Mechanical itch: a partly separate route

cards.front: Deleting Piezo1 in mouse peripheral neurons reduced mechanically evoked scratching, Piezo1 transcript appeared in 92 percent of Nppb-positive DRG neurons, and after combined Piezo1 and Piezo2 knockdown 32 of 33 cultured SST-marked neurons lacked mechanically activated responses. What follows about the peripheral split?
cards.back: A pruriceptor can itself transduce touch, so the chemical-versus-mechanical division is not an absolute split between peripheral cell types.
cards.quote: A pruriceptor can therefore transduce touch.
cards.section: Mechanical itch: a partly separate route

cards.front: In a primate in vivo, firing of eight histamine-responsive lumbar spinothalamic neurons during the first 10 seconds after scratching was 62 ± 8 percent of the pre-scratch level (mean ± SEM). For a cell firing 20 spikes per second before scratching, what mean rate does the central estimate predict, and by how much was firing suppressed?
cards.back: 0.62 × 20 = 12.4 spikes per second, a suppression of 38 percent of the pre-scratch level.
cards.quote: firing during the first 10 seconds after scratching was 62 ± 8 percent of the pre-scratch level
cards.section: Mechanical itch: ages, forces and counts

cards.front: In primate lumbar spinothalamic recordings, which activity did scratching suppress, and what is the limit of that measurement?
cards.back: Scratching suppressed histamine-evoked activity but not baseline or capsaicin-evoked activity. It is a firing measurement, not a reported sensation.
cards.quote: scratching suppressed histamine-evoked activity but not baseline or capsaicin-evoked activity
cards.section: Mechanical itch: a partly separate route

cards.front: What did epithelial TSLP do to sensory neurons in mouse DRG cultures, and how large was the responding fraction?
cards.back: It acted directly on TRPA1-positive sensory neurons, which responded with calcium; 4.1 ± 0.6 percent of cultured neurons responded.
cards.quote: Epithelial TSLP acted directly on TRPA1-positive sensory neurons in mouse DRG cultures, where the neurons responded with calcium
cards.section: Immune molecules can trigger or change gain

cards.front: Where does IL-31RA lie in sensory ganglia, and what happened to IL-31-evoked scratching in Trpv1- and Trpa1-deficient mice?
cards.back: IL-31RA lies largely in TRPV1-positive neurons in human donor and mouse DRG sections, and IL-31-evoked scratching was reduced in both Trpv1-deficient and Trpa1-deficient mice.
cards.quote: IL-31-evoked scratching was reduced in both Trpv1-deficient and Trpa1-deficient mice (Cevikbas and colleagues, 2014).
cards.section: Immune molecules can trigger or change gain

cards.front: IL-4 evokes calcium responses in cultured mouse and human sensory neurons, yet high-dose IL-4 injected into mouse skin did not by itself evoke acute scratching. Which interpretation is best supported, and why?
cards.back: IL-4 can sensitize neurons to pruritogens that were subthreshold alone without driving scratching by itself. Cellular responsiveness, acute behavioural output and sensitization are different claims: culture showed calcium responsiveness and sensitization, while skin injection did not show acute scratching.
cards.quote: Cellular responsiveness, acute behavioural output and sensitization are different claims.
cards.section: Immune molecules can trigger or change gain

cards.front: Deleting Il4ra or Jak1 in mouse sensory neurons reduced scratching in chronic-itch models. What general point does that support?
cards.back: A cytokine can change the gain of a sensory neuron without acting as an acute trigger, so signalling through this pathway matters even where the cytokine alone evokes no scratching.
cards.quote: A cytokine can therefore change gain without acting as an acute trigger.
cards.section: Immune molecules can trigger or change gain

cards.front: Which itch-pathway target does nemolizumab block, and which does dupilumab block?
cards.back: Nemolizumab blocks IL-31 receptor alpha. Dupilumab blocks IL-4R-alpha, the subunit shared by IL-4 and IL-13 signalling.
cards.quote: nemolizumab blocks IL-31 receptor alpha, and dupilumab blocks IL-4R-alpha, the subunit shared by IL-4 and IL-13 signalling
cards.section: Immune molecules can trigger or change gain

cards.front: Clinical chronic itch means itch lasting longer than {{c1::six weeks}}.
cards.quote: Clinical chronic itch means itch lasting longer than six weeks.
cards.section: Immune molecules can trigger or change gain

cards.front: A patient with chronic itch improves on an antibody that blocks IL-4R-alpha. Using this lesson's distinctions, what does the improvement not establish?
cards.back: It does not partition the drug's effect between neurons and immune cells, and it does not say whether the cytokine was acting as an acute trigger or as a gain setter. Those are separate claims that need the cellular and behavioural experiments, not the clinical response.
cards.quote: These studies do not partition a drug's effects between neurons and immune cells.
cards.section: Immune molecules can trigger or change gain

cards.front: A new chemical pruritogen makes mice scratch. Using this lesson's rules, which perturbations would place it in the framework, and what would each one license?
cards.back: Receptor or channel deletion shows which transduction route it needs; ablating a candidate afferent population tests necessity in those assays; a restricted rescue tests what that population can drive under one isolated input; blocking or ablating the spinal relay (NPRA, GRP, GRPR) tests the route downstream. Each perturbation supports only the link it actually tests, for the driver, age and assays used.
cards.quote: each perturbation supports only the link it actually tests

cards.front: Did the lesson establish what chemogenetically activating Merkel cells would do to touch-evoked scratching in aged mice?
cards.back: No. Activation lowered alloknesis only in the dry-skin model; applying that result to aged mice would be an untested extrapolation.
cards.quote: Chemogenetic activation of Merkel cells reduced alloknesis in a dry-skin model (Feng and colleagues, Science, 2018).
cards.section: Mechanical itch: a partly separate route
